pr_body: Solves several problems on stm32 lptimer
pr_comments:
thanks, 
Considering this PR with high interest for fixing the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/20991

This is valid  in a "ticked" mode, when CONFIG_TICKLESS_KERNEL is "n"
In case the CONFIG_TICKLESS_KERNEL is defined the testcase tests/kernel/timer/time_api still fails especially in test_timer_period_0.

I found these bugs by observing a time difference between the RTC and the lptimer when it both uses the LSI clock.
I used also a system tick of 8000 that divides 32000 (LSI frequency)
Did you check the time difference in case of LSE, if setting ` CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC + 1;`

Yes, I also observe a time difference with LSE without this correction.
I use 8192 for system tick.  We must have `(LPTIM_CLOCK % CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC) == 0' to not lose some clocks when calculating:
```
static void lptim_irq_handler(struct device *unused)
{
....
u32_t dticks = (autoreload
                             * CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC)
			     / LPTIM_CLOCK;
....
}
```

Testing on nucleo_wb55rg with CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK_LSE and CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=8192 gives an error on test tests/kernel/timer/timer_api
A lower value CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=4096  will pass this test.
However tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/  still fails if CONFIG_TIMESLICING=y

> Yes, I also observe a time difference with LSE without this correction.
> I use 8192 for system tick. We must have `(LPTIM_CLOCK % CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC) == 0' to not lose some clocks when calculating:
> 
> ```
> static void lptim_irq_handler(struct device *unused)
> {
> ....
> u32_t dticks = (autoreload
>                              * CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC)
> 			     / LPTIM_CLOCK;
> ....
> }
> ```

Yes, I think that's the reason why on the nRF52, we have:
```
CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_HW_CYCLES_PER_SEC=32768
CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=32768
```
Even if the ticks per sec value seems high, for a tickless kernel it is mostly defines the accuracy of the clock.
@FRASTM Why backup domain is reset in z_clock_driver_init? It removes my RTC config...

The sequence of setting the LSE as clock source is coming from stm32 applications.
This is not the case with LSI.

> The sequence of setting the LSE as clock source is coming from stm32 applications.
> This is not the case with LSI.

We don't need to reset backup domain to enable and set LSE for lptime:
```
Peripherals independent clock configuration register (RCC_CCIPR)

Bits 19:18 LPTIM1SEL[1:0]: Low power timer 1 clock source selection
These bits are set and cleared by software to select the LPTIM1 clock source.
00: PCLK selected as LPTIM1 clock
01: LSI clock selected as LPTIM1 clock
10: HSI16 clock selected as LPTIM1 clock
11: LSE clock selected as LPTIM1 clock
```
But this is the case for rtc only if the source change:
```
Backup domain control register (RCC_BDCR)

Bits 9:8 RTCSEL[1:0]: RTC clock source selection
Set by software to select the clock source for the RTC. Once the RTC clock source has been
selected, it cannot be changed anymore unless the Backup domain is reset, or unless a
failure is detected on LSE (LSECSSD is set). The BDRST bit can be used to reset them.
00: No clock
01: LSE oscillator clock used as RTC clock
10: LSI oscillator clock used as RTC clock
11: HSE oscillator clock divided by 32 used as RTC clock
```
So, in my opinion, we must remove the call to ```LL_RCC_ForceBackupDomainReset()``` and ```LL_RCC_ReleaseBackupDomainReset()``` here to avoid conflict with RTC counter.

I create a commit which remove ```LL_RCC_ForceBackupDomainReset()``` and ```LL_RCC_ReleaseBackupDomainReset()```
We probably have to do something similar for RTC counter driver (counter_ll_stm32_rtc)
@jdascenzio will you please create a PR to close #20991 separate from this one? That way we can lower the medium priority bug count to release 2.3.0

> > I create a commit which remove `LL_RCC_ForceBackupDomainReset()` and `LL_RCC_ReleaseBackupDomainReset()`
> > We probably have to do something similar for RTC counter driver (counter_ll_stm32_rtc)
> 
> @jdascenzio, To get this merged faster, I encourage you to create a dedicated PR, so you don't have to wait lptim fixes to be accepted. Also please create a matching issue as only bug fixes for known issues are being merged during the release process.

I create this PR #25576.

issue_context.title: test_timer_duration_period fails with stm32 lptimer
issue_context.body:
When the LPTIMER is enabled, the kernel test timer/timer_api fails in the 
"test_timer_duration_period: tdata.expire_cnt == 4 is false"


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Enable the LPTIMER in the proj.conf :
CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_TIMER=y
CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK_LSE=y
2. mkdir build; cd build
3. cmake -DBOARD=board\nucleo_l4r5zi
4. make
5. See error
"Assertion failed at ZEPHYR_BASE/tests/kernel/timer/timer_api/src/main.c:138: test_timer_duration_period: tdata.expire_cnt == 4 is false "
comments:
Due to the LPTIM clock source = LSE, the minimal tick period is set to 1000 per sec.
This makes one tick duration = about 33 lptim counting units

Note that the max possible timeout remains 2000ms , reached  when  the LPTIM counter = 0xFFFF

Applying the PR https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/24080
Plus a similar approach for the previous check in the testcase _test_timer_remaining_
zassert_true(rem_ticks <= (dur_ticks / 2) **+ 1** , NULL);

and it fixes for wb55 and l4r5 when the STM32_LPTIM_TIMER is defined
@erwango It doesn't seem this actually has a PR does it?
@carlescufi #20992 should be the one closing this.

review_comments: However, with `CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC - 1;`  the testcase tests/kernel/timer/timer_api/ test_timer_period_0 still fails.
